---
title: as-factor
subtitle: Coerce a column to string factors, or tag an aesthetic as discrete.
category: Core
since: 0.1.0
engine: markdown
---


Two call forms:
when given `(data, col)` it returns a new dataset with `col` stringified in
every row; when given `(col)` alone it returns a mapping-ref annotation
that [`aes`](aes.qmd) accepts in place of a column name, forcing the scale system to
treat that channel as discrete.

## Usage

```typst
as-factor(data, col)
```

```typst
as-factor(col)
```

## Arities

- `as-factor(data, col)`: Return a new dataset with `col` coerced to strings (preserving `none`).
- `as-factor(col)`: Return a `mapping-ref` dict tagging `col` as discrete for [`aes`](aes.qmd).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `..args` |  | Either `(data, col)` or `(col)`. See arities. |

## Returns

New dataset (2-arg) or mapping-ref dict (1-arg).

## Examples

```{typst}
//| output-filename: "/assets/typst-render/as-factor-1.svg"
//| width: 10cm
//| height: 6cm
#let iris = (
  (sl: 5.1, sp: 1),
  (sl: 7.0, sp: 2),
  (sl: 6.3, sp: 3),
)
#plot(
  data: iris,
  mapping: aes(x: as-factor("sp"), y: "sl", fill: as-factor("sp")),
  layers: (geom-col(),),
)
```
